notes.claim: In a composition of functions the output of one function becomes the input of another.
For differential-pressure flow, a signal that is 50% pressure difference at 12 mA goes through a square root to become 71% flow: one function's output feeds the next.
The SQA HN Engineering Mathematics unit includes deriving and evaluating composite functions.
UK books write the composite f(g(x)) as fg(x), found by working out g(x) first and then substituting it into f (Bitesize, notes 4.7; for i7).
For a DP flow meter the square root is taken in the transmitter or in the controller, but not both; taking it in both gives the wrong flow (Control Engineering, notes 7.6; for i7).

sources.title: 3.4 Composition of Functions - College Algebra 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: The process of combining functions so that the output of one function becomes the input of another is known as a composition of functions

sources.title: Square root scaling for differential pressure flowmeters - Control Engineering
sources.quote: Regardless of the type of obstruction (orifice plate, Venturi or Pitot tube, etc), the DP is proportional to the square of the flow. Therefore the system must scale flow from the square root of the DP.

sources.title: Square root scaling for differential pressure flowmeters - Control Engineering
sources.quote: But the root of a number from 0-1 is larger: √0.5 = 0.707. So if there is a 12 mA signal from the DP cell, that’s 50% DP, but 71% flow rate.

sources.quote: 𝑓𝑔(𝑥) is calculated by finding 𝑔(𝑥) first, and then substituting this into the function 𝑓.

sources.title: Square root scaling for differential pressure flowmeters - Control Engineering
sources.quote: The square root for DP-based flow can be taken either in the transmitter or in the controller (but not both).
